summary_paragraph: A female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for fever, shortness of breath, and productive cough. She was evaluated for possible pneumonia and cardiac ischemia due to new ST changes on ECG, but serial troponins remained stable within her baseline. A chest X-ray showed mild volume overload, and a small possible infiltrate was noted. She was treated with levofloxacin for community-acquired pneumonia. Her symptoms improved during the stay, and she remained hemodynamically stable. She also had transiently elevated liver enzymes, which trended downward without intervention, and an ultrasound revealed no acute abdominal pathology. She was discharged home on a short course of antibiotics and adjusted doses of lisinopril and metoprolol, with instructions to follow up on liver function tests.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
